summary: Ramaswamy, Simons and Banerjee represent each regular distribution as a family of line segments (FALLS), so the data to move between two processor sets is an intersection of such families. They add a locality-aware packing scheme and a contention-reducing send order, and report Intel Paragon timings showing that these optimizations cut redistribution time.
why_read: It explains concretely how a runtime library can compute which elements move between arbitrary processor subsets for regular distributions.
main_contribution: A FALLS representation and period-based intersection algorithm for regular distributions, with locality-aware packing and a contention-reducing schedule for redistribution between arbitrary processor sets.
main_limitation: Only regular per-dimension distributions and whole-array redistribution are handled, without array reshaping, and the results come from one machine with the authors' earlier algorithm as the only baseline.
evaluation_method: Wall-clock timings of three algorithm variants on the Intel Paragon over 27 cases, plus measured analysis overhead.
benchmarks: 27 array redistributions of 100x100, 200x200 and 400x400 arrays on the Intel Paragon
